Scribes, illuminators, and scholars held such stones directly over manuscript '''pages''' as an aid in seeing what was being written, drawn, or read.}} # One side of a paper [[leaf]] in a bound document. #: {{syn|en|folio|side}} # {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[collective]] [[memory]]; [[noteworthy]] [[event]]; [[memorable]] [[episode]]. #: {{uxi|en|a '''page''' from history}} # {{lb|en|typesetting}} The [[type]] set up for [[print]]ing a page. # {{lb|en|computing}} A [[screenful]] of [[text]] and possibly other content; especially, the digital simulation of one side of a paper leaf. #: {{hypo|en|help page|man page}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|author=Maria Langer|title=Mac OS X 10.2 Advanced|page=44|text=To view man '''pages''' for a command: Type man followed by the name of the command (for example, man ls), and press Return. {{...}} To view the next '''page''': Press Spacebar. {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== {{etymon|en|id=servant}} From {{der|en|fro|page}}, possibly via {{der|en|it|paggio}}, from {{der|en|la-med|pagius||servant}}, probably from {{der|en|grc|παιδίον||boy, lad}}, from {{m|grc|παῖς||child}}; some sources consider this unlikely and suggest instead {{der|en|la|pagus||countryside}}, in sense of "boy from the rural regions". Used in English from the 13th century onwards. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|historical}} A [[serve|serving]] boy; a youth attending a person of high degree, especially at [[court]]s, often as a position of honor and education. #: {{syn|en|pageboy}} # {{lb|en|British}} A [[youth]] employed for doing [[errand]]s, waiting on the door, and similar service in households. # {{lb|en|US|Canada}} A [[boy]] or [[girl]] employed to wait upon the members of a legislative body. # {{lb|en|in libraries}} An [[employee]] whose main purpose is to replace materials that have either been [[checked out]] or otherwise moved, back to their shelves. # A [[contrivance]], such as a [[band]], [[pin]], [[snap]], or the like, to hold the [[skirt]] of a woman’s dress from the ground. # A [[track]] along which [[pallet]]s carrying newly molded [[brick]]s are conveyed to the [[hack]]. # {{lb|en|telecommunications|dated}} A [[message]] sent to someone's [[pager]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1991|author=w:Stephen King|title=w:Needful Things|page=355|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/lccn_051488024958_36j/page/355/mode/1up|text=Before he could bring it down, the pager clipped to his belt went off. {{...}} If you were a lawyer or a business executive, maybe you could afford to ignore your '''pages''' for a while, but when you were a County Sheriff—and one who was elected rather than appointed—there wasn't much question about priorities.}} #
